A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniMMAD. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original anomaly-detection results, component ablations, continual-learning experiments, and efficiency measurements, with additional results in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds specialized-versus-unified training comparisons and results against CCL.

M1.justification: The encoder, FCM, cross-conditioned MoE, hierarchical experts, losses, and inference procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Equations 1–4. The added description of inter-modal prior averaging supplies implementation detail without establishing a procedural revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine datasets, modalities, classes, and detection/localization tasks. Removing 'Infrared' from the MVTec-3D dataset-table entry corrects a description already presented as RGB-D elsewhere in v1; it does not establish changed experimental coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds CCL to the MVTec-AD/VisA comparison in Appendix Table 7. It removes UniNet from the quantitative UniMed comparisons in Tables 1–2 and the corresponding appendix table, although UniNet remains displayed in Figure 5. Other comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New Table 5 introduces specialized-versus-unified training controls for UniMMAD and the existing baseline. Table 6 adds FLOPs as an efficiency metric. Previously stated training budgets, resolutions, backbones, and detection metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 5 tests the performance cost of unified training: mean image AUROC falls from 81.2 to 75.6 for the baseline, versus 91.2 to 91.1 for UniMMAD. Existing component ablations, continual-learning tests, expert-count and backbone/resolution analyses, and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for the experimental results. The added comparisons continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: VisA pixel-level results are substantially revised in Table 3 and v1 Appendix Table 11/v2 Table 13. In Table 3, UniMMAD's MF1/AUPRO changes from 44.9/47.2 to 47.2/91.3, while INP-Former's changes from 40.5/44.4 to 44.4/91.5, reversing their reported AUPRO ranking. ViTAD's MVTec-AD pixel results change from 95.9/49.8/89.4 to 97.1/57.0/90.9. Training-control, CCL, and FLOPs results are added, and UniNet results are removed. These are reporting revisions and additions, not established improvements from a changed method.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 retain the same load-balancing loss, expert composition, reconstruction loss, and anomaly-score definitions. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs; the wording and notation refinements introduce no substantive mathematical change.

C1.justification: The abstract explicitly restricts the approximately 75% parameter-saving claim to MoE parameters. The central claims about unified detection, dataset breadth, state-of-the-art performance, continual learning, and efficient inference otherwise remain intact.

C2.justification: The new 'Unified vs. Specialized' discussion attributes stability under unified training to adaptive routing that reduces domain conflicts, and interprets gains on MulSen-AD and BraTS as benefits for data-scarce infrared and complex multimodal inputs. Existing interpretations are largely retained, with no substantive new limitations discussion.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 newly documents refinement using inter-modal prior averages. Conversely, the efficiency-table caption drops v1's identification of MVTec-3D as the measurement dataset and MulSen-AD as the exception for MulSen-TripleAD. Training hyperparameters, hardware, and the repository link target remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the CCL reference and comparison and removes the UniNet reference. The introduction also refines its characterization of earlier approaches toward fixed modality combinations rather than universally single-class models. The broader related-work coverage and positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: There are localized introduction rewrites, method-description clarifications, author-affiliation and contribution-label edits, and a short new appendix comparison section. The main section sequence and most explanatory prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a document-wide visual redesign with institutional branding, a boxed full-width abstract, colored headings, running headers, and extensive figure/table relocation and resizing. Figure 5 is restyled, a training-control table is added, Table 3 is additionally displayed with CCL, and the efficiency table gains a FLOPs column. Existing appendix qualitative panels are retained.

improvement.justification: The training controls and CCL comparison strengthen empirical support for the existing contribution. v2 also reconciles ViTAD's MVTec-AD summary with appendix results and corrects the '75% of parameters' wording to '75% fewer.' These gains are limited by remaining reporting problems: the retained 10.8% VisA improvement claim conflicts with the revised 47.2 versus 44.4 MF1 values, and the efficiency table loses dataset context and introduces incorrect memory/parameter unit labels.
